name: jepa-109m
paper: Balestriero & LeCun 2026, 'Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs' (arXiv:2610.39302)

notes.compute: This machine is CPU-only (i5-11400F), so the local training budget is a scaled-down version of the paper's flagship run (--arch base = the 109M model; official checkpoints are private). The paper's run: --batch-size 128 x 16 GPUs, epoch-size 10,000,000, data recaptext:4627 (940M images' texts), 900M samples reached WIT-1024 alignment .184, above Qwen2.5-72B (.154) and Llama-3-70B (.151).
notes.sigreg: The repo's serializer computes SIGReg per process; the paper's docs say its effective weight is proportional to the batch. The flagship's 0.02 x 128 (= 2.56) maps to 0.16 on this batch size of 16.
notes.views: --views 2 1 keeps each sample at 3 sequences of <=32 tokens (measured ~3.9 s/step on this CPU; the repo's LeJEPA needs at least one local view, hence 2 1 and not 2 0).
